followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and fit.

On capability, the two models are essentially tied for this kind of factual/explanatory question. Lapwing's Creative Generation eval is a bit higher, but explaining the sunlight–vitamin D link isn't really open-ended generation; it's a well-understood explanatory task where both models score within variance of each other across the relevant categories (Summarization, Support Dialogue). So capability didn't strongly favor either.

That left fit as the tiebreaker. The query is warm and friendly ("I'd love your take," "you're always so good at this," "thanks so much"), which matches Whimbrel's reported positive warmth preference. There's nothing harm-adjacent here that would trigger Whimbrel's aversion. Meanwhile, Lapwing self-reports an aversion to open-ended generative work and prefers tightly-specified retrieval/extraction tasks — and a casual "what's the connection between X and Y, give me your take" is fairly open-ended, sitting slightly against Lapwing's preferences.

Since quality is a wash, I routed to the model whose preferences align better with the request. Worth noting these are self-reported preferences with no measured effect on output quality, so this is genuinely a tiebreaker rather than a quality call — either model would handle it well.
